title: audio: ensure volume and mute changes apply to bluetooth sinks
head: 1e703c922d90
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: two findings: toggleOutputMute double toggle (visible), channel balance flattening (collapsed)

leads.summary: Bluetooth route mute does not share the missing-volumeStep bug; a second pactl toggle can undo the working Quickshell mute write
leads.consequence: For a bound sink whose Quickshell mute write reaches the server before detached pactl runs, clicking the output mute control sends mute=true followed by toggle, leaving output unmuted. Unmute behaves symmetrically, and with variable scheduling can appear to briefly change then rebound. Missing BlueZ volumeStep alone does not explain a mute failure. Issue applies to routed Bluetooth and ordinary sinks on which the first write succeeds. Use one authoritative mute write, preferably an absolute requested state through pactl for the sinks needing the fallback, instead of pairing Quickshell setMuted with pactl toggle.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus finding 1 and mute root-cause note; published

leads.summary: Dragging or scrolling output volume discards a user's channel balance
leads.consequence: On a stereo/multichannel sink whose channels are deliberately unequal, the new single percentage pactl write broadcasts the same value to every channel. In an isolated two-channel sink, 20%/80% became 50%/50% after one 50% output update. Quickshell's previous setter scales each channel relative to its previous volume; even when it succeeds, the subsequent pactl call flattens the balance. This can make one side unexpectedly louder and erase an accessibility or speaker-alignment setting on every panel wheel, keyboard, or slider change. Preserve the existing channel ratios when issuing a fallback backend write (or explicitly expose balance policy).

leads.summary: After an output switch, stale resolved sink names can make pactl write a removed or wrong sink
leads.consequence: When default switches from bluez_output.old to bluez_output.new while the async output-sink resolver has not finished, volumeSink falls back to the new live node once old is removed, but targetSink unconditionally chooses the nonempty cached name of old. An output slider change now shows 75% on new while it dispatches pactl to old (which fails if removed, or changes an unintended output if still present). This defeats the Bluetooth fallback precisely during reconnect/profile or output switching, and the detached error is not surfaced; next successful resolver run may correct it, with a 15-second retry timer. Clear or validate the cached name on sink change and choose a single currently resolved target for the QML property and pactl write.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus 'transient mismatch' observation; transient, pre-existing resolver behavior; not published

leads.summary: Five non-stacked open PRs overlap changed audio panel functions and cannot be combined without selecting competing behavior
leads.consequence: #13004 and #13099 already implement serialized/coalesced pactl output writes and conflict with this PR's detached write in setOutputVolume; accepting this PR's branch removes their last-write-wins behavior and breaks #13099's explicit no-detached-write assertion. #7812 replaces the same volume and mute functions with wpctl, three conflicts. #8871 raises maximum volume to 125% and conflicts on the new clamp: taking only its slider maximum leaves a 125% slider that the reviewed Math.min(1, v) caps at 100%; taking only this PR's setter loses the intended 125% setting. #7714 intentionally changes the hero to output-only mute and removes toggleAllMuted, conflicting with this PR's added hero mute backend path. All five heads diverge from this one (not stacked). Coordinate or supersede these proposals, preserving selected semantics and tests, before merging.
leads.triage: verified_partially_published; Coordinator verified with gh: all open; #13004 and #13099 change setOutputVolume for issue #12886 (published in Details). #8871 clamp point: 100% clamp predates this PR (unchanged line), not published. #7812/#7714 overlap not published.

H03 uses the actual extracted QML functions with a recorded detached-argv stub, not a physical reconnect.

The package lists do not pin dependency versions (install/omarchy-base.packages:113,141 and install/omarchy-other.packages:14,39). Source verification uses Quickshell v0.3.1, PipeWire v1.6.8 and pactl v17.0, and master Quickshell has a missing-volumeStep fix; which exact binary an upgraded user has is not fixed by this repository.

Existing test/shell.d/audio-test.sh passes at head and quattro with 20 printed assertions but imports only Model.js, so passing does not validate any changed QML path. No new test was added, and this is a test-validity caveat rather than a standalone generic issue.

issues.requirement: Readable comments (2026-09-28): every finding the review reproduced needs a collapsed Reproducer block with a self-contained runnable reproducer and its actual output.
issues.excerpt: <details><summary>Reproducer (runtime check)</summary> ... The harness copies the `sink`/`volumeSink`/`outputVolume` declarations ... ## Manual check on a live system (not run for this review)
issues.correction: The channel-balance finding is presented as reproduced: it has a runtime table of merge-base and head results. Its Reproducer block only describes the harness in prose. The only commands it gives are manual steps marked as not run, so the output shown does not come from any reproducer in the draft. Add a self-contained runnable reproducer, for example a test in the style of `test/shell.d/`, together with its actual output at the reviewed head, and label the summary 'fails at 1e703c92'. If no runnable reproducer exists, state in the finding text that the harness is not included, and relabel the block as Details rather than Reproducer.
